No other diagnosis (e.g., PCD, CF, immunodeficiency) is supported by any positive test or defining clinical feature in the summary — only by absence of alternatives and need for exclusion.

[EVIDENCE]  
- 11-year history of chronic, aggressive, productive cough  
- Thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum  
- Multiple episodes of antibiotic-treated bronchitis  
- Post-bronchodilator spirometry shows ↓ FVC and ↓ FEV1 with ✅ normal FEV1/FVC ratio  
- Sputum culture shows heavy growth of non-specific bacteria  
- No *M. tuberculosis* or fungi identified in sputum culture  
- Provisional working diagnosis explicitly identifies “chronic suppurative airway disease, highly suspicious for … bronchiectasis”  

[GAPS]  
- High-resolution chest CT — required to confirm presence, pattern, and extent of bronchiectasis  
- Sweat chloride test and/or CFTR genetic testing — to exclude cystic fibrosis  
- Nasal nitric oxide (nNO) level — to screen for primary ciliary dyskinesia  
- Quantitative immunoglobulins and IgG subclasses — to assess for humoral immunodeficiency  
- Alpha-1 antitrypsin level and Pi phenotype — to exclude alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Bronchiectasis
